packs.title: Rooms without Walls
packs.promise: Read the city through fences, open spaces and the landscapes around art.

q.s: Find the small lines that organize a bright facade.
st: Observe from the public sidewalk, away from the restaurant’s entrance and arriving guests.
Find a large color area, a narrow contrasting trim line and a small repeated exterior detail.
Record how those three sizes work together; choose the detail you might otherwise have missed.

q.s: Find three details that help an open space work.
st: Enter by an open public path or choose a view from the sidewalk.
Find something that guides movement, something that offers rest and something that creates shade.
Make a three-item toolkit for the square and choose the item you would miss most.

q.s: Collect the landscape around a sculpture.
st: Use an open garden path and select any outdoor sculpture visible without entering planted areas.
Find three surrounding elements: a ground surface, a growing form and an open gap.
Describe how one of these changes your impression of the sculpture without touching it.

packs.title: River & Revelations
packs.promise: Read the Quarter’s small details, then let the river change your view.

q.s: Find three motifs hiding inside the repetition.
st: From the public sidewalk along one Pontalba edge of Jackson Square, look up at the ironwork without approaching a doorway or private balcony.
Find three distinct motifs: a curve, an angular shape, and a repeating unit. They can all come from one clear view.
Give each motif a simple nickname based on its shape. Compare how closely spaced and open areas change the pattern.
Save your three motifs and the one you would recognize again. A written description is enough; no rubbing or touching is involved.

q.s: Give one architectural detail a tiny fictional adventure.
st: Choose a doorway shape, shutter, balcony curve, or other exterior detail visible from a clear public spot near Royal and Toulouse.
Invent a three-sentence story in which that object wants something, encounters a small complication, and ends somewhere emotionally different. Keep it clearly your imagination.
Include two visible details from the real object, such as its color and a chipped edge. Do not invent a real resident’s life, a building’s history, or a local legend.
Save the story in a field note, or photograph the object and keep the story as a private thought. There is no performance to give.

q.s: Watch one skyline detail change its place during a ferry crossing.
st: Check the RTA’s current Canal–Algiers Point ferry alerts, departure information, fare, accessible boarding, and return service before entering the terminal. Choose the same-bank alternative if the trip does not suit you.
From a safe public viewpoint, choose a visible building or skyline shape to remember. Board only when directed; settle before observing through a window or from an authorized deck area.

After arriving at Algiers Point and clearing the terminal, find your chosen shape again if visible. Describe how its size or relation to the water has changed; if it disappears, describe what replaced it in the view.
Save the comparison and confirm your next or return journey. The quest is complete after one crossing; the rest of this chapter is optional.
